message.content:
Here are some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling:

| Title | Year Published | Notes |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (also *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | First book in the Harry Potter series; introduces the wizarding world. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Second installment; expands on Hogwarts lore. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Introduces Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | Features the Triwizard Tournament. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Focuses on the formation of Dumbledore’s Army. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half‑Blood Prince** | 2005 | Provides backstory on Voldemort’s rise. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | Concludes the epic saga. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel, dealing with political intrigue in a small town. |
| **The Cuckoo’s Calling** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2013 | Debut of the detective series featuring private investigator Cormoran Strike. |
| **The Silkworm** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2014 | Second book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Career of Evil** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2015 | Third installment in the Strike series. |
| **Lethal White** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2018 | Fourth book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Troubled Blood** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2020 | Fifth book in the Strike series. |

These titles have achieved widespread popularity, sold millions of copies worldwide, and have been adapted into blockbuster films (the Harry Potter movies) and a successful television series (Cormoran Strike).
